WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


Key Overview:
As a Member of Technical Staff in Post-Training, you will train our large language models (LLMs) with reinforcement learning and develop methods that help them generalize beyond the distribution they were trained on. You will design the training recipes, environments, and evaluations that tell us whether a model has truly learned a skill or has only fitted its training tasks, and turn what works into the recipes behind our production models. You will work closely with the post-training data infrastructure, evaluation, and pre-training teams.

Key Responsibilities

 - Design, run, and analyse large-scale RL post-training experiments (e.g., RLHF, RL from verifiable rewards).

 - Research and develop methods that improve out-of-distribution generalization, such as reward design, environment and task diversity, curricula, and regularization.

 - Build held-out evaluations that measure generalization to unseen tasks, domains, and formats, and that catch reward hacking and benchmark overfitting.

 - Diagnose training dynamics and failure modes, including instability, reward over-optimization, and capability regressions.

 - Turn successful research into robust, reproducible training recipes for production models.


Qualifications

 - Strong research and software engineering skills, with hands-on experience training LLMs.

 - Experience applying reinforcement learning to LLMs (e.g., PPO, GRPO, RLHF, RLVR), ideally at scale.

 - Track record of work on generalization, robustness, or distribution shift, through publications or shipped models.

 - Rigorous experimental practice: clean ablations, careful controls, and sound conclusions from noisy results.

 - Experience with distributed training (e.g., JAX, PyTorch, FSDP, Megatron) is a plus.

 - Excellent communication skills.

 - Deep understanding of data quality principles and best practices: demonstrates willingness to dive deep into data while possessing strong intuition for assessing the quality of datasets and anticipating how different data characteristics will impact model training outcomes.
   

Working Location
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

 




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.

Afin de maintenir cette dynamique de croissance et de libérer de la capacité décisionnelle au sein de l'organisation commerciale globale, nous créons un poste de direction stratégique dédié afin de piloter, développer et commercialiser nos occasions dans les nouveaux marchés verticaux au Canada et à l'international.

 Relevant directement du directeur principal des revenus (Chief Revenue Officer - CRO), ce rôle se situe à la croisée de l'exécution commerciale traditionnelle, de la définition de stratégies de haut niveau, de l'alignement produit, de la coordination interfonctionnelle et de l'exécution de la stratégie de commercialisation (GTM). Vous assumerez la responsabilité globale du développement des marchés secondaires, de l'évaluation des dynamiques de marché, de la mise en place des rythmes opérationnels et du positionnement de Paramount Commerce en tant que chef de file dans les secteurs technologiques et fintech adjacents.

 Stratégie d'investissement produit : Analyser les métriques du pipeline et les rétroactions du marché pour orienter les orientations produit de haut niveau et préconiser les investissements produit nécessaires.
 Responsabilité directe des revenus : Assumer la responsabilité directe d'un quota de revenus verticaux, en pilotant les cycles de vente de bout en bout, de la stratégie initiale jusqu'à l'exécution et la réalisation des objectifs de revenus dans les secteurs à forte croissance.
 2. Leadership d'exécution et alignement interfonctionnel 
 Exécution opérationnelle : Traduire la vision stratégique en feuilles de route commerciales concrètes, en éliminant les obstacles à l'exécution entre les équipes Produit, Opérations, Marketing et Commerciales.
 Gouvernance et imputabilité : Établir des rythmes opérationnels rigoureux, des cadres d'indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), des tableaux de bord de gestion de la performance et des rapports destinés à la direction pour la croissance des nouveaux marchés.

 Soutien commercial : Compléter l'équipe de développement des affaires principale en intervenant sur des occasions stratégiques complexes à haute valeur ajoutée et dans des fonctions de conseil.

 Qualifications et expérience

Founded in 2019, Phoenix is building the most trusted telehealth platform in Canada, making specialist healthcare accessible to every Canadian, wherever they are. Our platform breaks down barriers to care, empowering patients to take control of their health with personalized treatment options and the guidance of licensed providers.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an Organic Growth Manager to help us expand our reach, impact, and grow our patient-base. In this role, you'll turn search data, audience insights, and channel experimentation into strategies that drive awareness, trust, and growth for our brand.

As our Organic Growth Manager, you'll own the engine that helps men discover accessible, stigma-free care for conditions like erectile dysfunction, hair loss, weight management, and testosterone optimization. You'll collaborate closely with marketing, product, and content teams to improve visibility, authority, and performance across organic channels. Together, you'll push organic growth across every channel, from traditional search to AI-powered discovery to social channels.

This role is as much about building the foundation as it is about driving results. You'll have the autonomy to define the strategy, run the experiments, and set the standard for how Phoenix grows organically. Your ability to blend strategic thinking with hands-on execution will directly shape how we attract, educate, and convert our customers.




WHAT YOU’LL DO TO SUPPORT THE COMPANY MISSION

 - Develop and execute an organic growth strategy across SEO, content distribution, and emerging AI-era discovery channels that drives qualified traffic and user acquisition across all key men's health categories.

 - Lead SEO strategy with a strong grounding in on-page, off-page, and technical fundamentals and an eye toward what comes next, including AEO and GEO frameworks.

 - Conduct keyword and phrasing research alongside competitive analysis to uncover opportunities, inform content, and guide long-term growth.

 - Ensure every article, landing page, and campaign is built on strong organic fundamentals and positioned for both traditional and AI-driven search.

 - Identify and launch non-traditional, non-paid growth channels including, but not limited to, community-led strategies on platforms like Reddit, highly shareable patient stories and testimonials, or owned content formats that earn attention rather than buy it.

 - Use data and creativity together to test unconventional ideas, learn fast, and double down on what works.

 - Monitor performance and report on KPIs including rankings, organic traffic, share of voice, and conversion rates.

 - Stay ahead of algorithm updates, AI search evolution, and industry trends to keep our organic strategy sharp and adaptive.

 - Experiment with new tools, AI integrations, and automation to improve efficiency and scalability across organic channels.

 - Work closely with Marketing, Product, and Engineering teams to test ideas quickly, share feedback openly, and build strategies that move fast and learn faster.

 - 4–6+ years of organic growth marketing experience, ideally with SEO strategy skills, in a DTC, tech, or healthcare environment.

 - A strong SEO foundation and a track record of going beyond it. You've driven organic growth across channels, not just rankings.

 - A growth hacker's mindset. You're as comfortable mining data for insight as you are pitching a scrappy idea nobody's tried yet.

 - Demonstrable, owned results. You can point to specific outcomes you drove, not just programs you were part of.

 - Experience building something from the ground up. Whether it’s been a channel, a strategy, a playbook, you don't need a roadmap to get started.

 - Familiarity with AEO and GEO frameworks and how AI-era search is reshaping organic discovery.

 - Hands-on experience with tools like Google Analytics (GA4), Search Console, Ahrefs, SEMrush, and Screaming Frog.

WHY WORK AT PHOENIX?

 - A Rewarding Mission: Through our asynchronous care model, Phoenix is reimagining patient-centric care for Canadians across the country by making diagnoses and treatment delivery faster, more accessible, and completely discreet.

About Jacuzzi Group 
 Jacuzzi Group is a leading global manufacturer of hot tubs, swim spas, saunas, and pool equipment. More than four thousand global employees work across our portfolio of brands, including Jacuzzi, Sundance Spas, Hydropool Swim Spas and Hot Tubs, DreamMaker, and more.
 With a presence in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Italy, the United Kingdom, France, Brazil, Chile, and Australia, we have more than 65 years of experience delivering innovative wellness products to our consumers across our many brands.
 Position Overview 
 Jacuzzi Group is seeking a Sales Manager to drive sales growth within an assigned territory. This role manages a network of dealers while identifying and developing new market opportunities for Jacuzzi, Hydropool, DreamMaker, and Sundance Spas, promoting and selling spas, swim spas, saunas, and cold plunge tubs. The Sales Manager is accountable for achieving both monthly and annual sales goals.
 This is a field-based role covering the Northern Ontario, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba area, with 50–60% travel by car.
 Who You Are 
 You are a results-driven field sales professional with a track record of consistently meeting your goals. You build strong, lasting relationships with dealers, enjoy teaching others how to sell and succeed, and are just as comfortable growing existing accounts as you are prospecting for new ones. You are self-motivated, organized, and at home on the road.
 What You'll Do

 What You Bring 
 Required

 •       Proven success consistently meeting sales goals
 •       Ability to travel 50–60% by car, including some overnights as required by regional geography
 •       Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint
 •       Strong written and verbal communication skills
 •       Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities with strong attention to detail
   Preferred 
 •       Experience selling to a dealer or channel network
 •       Physical products sales experience; high-ticket sales experience 
 •       Experience in a private equity-backed or high-growth company
 The statements in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required. 
 What We Offer 
 Jacuzzi Group offers a competitive total compensation package. This position includes a base salary of $90,000+ annually (depending on experience), as well as eligibility for an annual performance-based bonus program, providing the opportunity to earn additional compensation tied to individual and company results.

 This is a field-based role covering the Northern Ontario, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba area. Expect 50–60% field travel by car, including overnight stays when required by regional geography.
 Equal Opportunity Employer

 VP, Business Group Information Security Officer, SLAM (BG CISO)  
 Job Purpose  
 The Vice-President, Business Group Information Security Officer, SLAM (BG CISO) serves as a senior security leader and partner to the Business Group leadership team and Business Group President.  Acting as the senior security executive for the Business Group and the primary bridge between the business and enterprise Security function, the BG CISO provides independent oversight and challenge of cyber risk, resilience and security outcomes across the business group. 
 The BG CISO is accountable for cyber risk, resilience, and security outcomes for Sun Life Asset Management, a global asset management platform with approximately $1.6 trillion in AUM, established to strengthen collaboration across MFS Investment Management, SLC Management, Sun Life’s stake in Aditya Birla Sun Life Asset Management, the pension risk transfer business and the broader company.  
 Reporting directly to the global Chief Security Officer, this role is responsible for ongoing emphasis on ensuring full capabilities across Sun Life Asset Management are consistently leveraged to deliver value and innovation.  Direct and indirect reports include a team of ~ 10 security leads and advisors aligned to Asset Management business priorities, product/platform risk, incident readiness, and stakeholder engagement.  
 The BG CISO partners closely with executives, technology leaders, risk partners, and the enterprise security team to protect critical assets, enable innovation, strengthen resilience, and ensure risks are understood and managed within the organization's risk appetite. The BG CISO is accountable for providing independent business-aligned security oversight while enabling growth, innovation and transformation across the Business Group. The role translates complex cyber and security risks into business impacts and shapes strategy, investments, priorities, and operating decisions across the Business Group.  
 Scope, Decision Authority and Key Interfaces  
 The Vice-President, Business Group Information Security Officer serves as the senior security executive and trusted advisor to the Business Group President and leadership team. The role is accountable for cyber risk oversight, executive advisory services, security governance, resilience alignment, regulatory engagement, and independent challenge across the assigned business group. The Vice-President translates enterprise security strategy into business-relevant actions while ensuring cyber risk, resilience, regulatory obligations, and security priorities are appropriately considered within business decisions and transformation initiatives.  
 The Vice-President has delegated authority to establish business-group security governance routines, direct security assessments, challenge risk decisions, require remediation planning, recommend security investment priorities, and escalate material cyber and resilience concerns through appropriate governance channels. Within approved authorities, the role provides independent advice and challenge regarding cyber risk, resilience, technology transformation, regulatory obligations, third-party risk, and risk acceptance decisions. Where management disagreement exists regarding material cyber risk acceptance, the matter will be escalated to the Global Chief Information Security Officer for review and discussion with the applicable Business Group President before a final decision is made. 
 The role is accountable for business-group security oversight, executive advisory services, risk escalation, independent challenge, alignment of enterprise security services to business priorities, and operational ownership of Business Group Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) platforms and associated security outcomes. The role does not own enterprise cyber defence operations, enterprise security platform engineering, vulnerability remediation, incident response operations, or second-line risk oversight except where responsibilities are expressly assigned. The Vice-President works closely with Enterprise Security leaders to ensure Business Group CIAM capabilities remain aligned with enterprise architecture, security standards, resilience requirements, and regulatory obligations. 
 Matters escalated to the Chief Information Security Officer would typically include significant cyber or operational resilience concerns, material breaches of risk appetite, major regulatory matters, unresolved management actions, significant third-party security issues, material client commitments, or disagreements regarding risk acceptance, prioritization, or investment decisions. 
 Major Accountabilities   
 Strategic Security Leadership and Vision  
 Serve as the primary Security advisor to the Business Group executive team and Business Group President. 
 Accountable for defining and driving the Business Group security strategy, aligned to enterprise security priorities and business objectives. 
 Ensure security considerations are integrated into business strategy, transformation initiatives, digital strategies, and operational decision-making. 
 Report significant changes in risk to appropriate levels of leadership on a periodic and event-driven basis.  
 Exercise independent challenge and escalate material cyber, technology, resilience and security risks through appropriate governance forums when risk exposure exceeds established risk appetite or remediation commitments are not achieved.  
 Deliver timely insights and data to enable informed executive decision-making, prioritization, and risk-based trade-offs.  
 Influence and shape multi-year security, resilience, and technology risk investment strategies, ensuring resource allocation aligns with business priorities, regulatory expectations and evolving threat landscapes.  
 Identify emerging threats, trends, and regulatory developments that may impact the Business Group and proactively develop mitigation strategies. 
 Business Partnership & Influence  
 Build trusted relationships with business and technology executives. 
 Act as the voice of the Business Group within the CISO organization and as the voice of the CISO organization within the Business Group. 
 Facilitate effective collaboration between business stakeholders and enterprise security teams. 
 Influence business group investment priorities and strategic trade-offs related to cyber risk, resilience, regulatory obligations, and secure technology adoption 
 Cyber Risk Management  
 Accountable for the Business Group’s cyber risk posture, control effectiveness and security outcomes, ensuring material risks are identified, assessed, escalated, remediated, or formally accepted through appropriate governance and in alignment with enterprise risk appetite. 
 Facilitate cyber risk assessments across application/platform/system levels to identify vulnerabilities and potential threats, analyze impacts, and recommend protection required based on threat modeling. 
 Support business leaders in making informed risk decisions consistent with enterprise policies and risk appetite. 
 Work with the Global Cyber threat intelligence team and monitor evolving threat landscapes and advise leaders on risk implications and required actions. 
 Provide oversight of BG specific third-party cyber risk related to critical vendors, strategic partners, outsourced services, and technology providers, ensuring security risks are appropriately identified, assessed, governed, monitored and escalated as appropriate.  
 Provide independent security advice on material risk acceptance decisions and ensure risks exceeding approved appetite or delegated authority are escalated to the appropriate enterprise and business governance forums.  
 Governance, Regulatory & Compliance  
 Lead security governance activities within the Business Group. 
 Oversee regular reporting and ensure alignment to global functional teams 
 Represent Security on business governance forums, executive committees, and risk councils. 
 Ensure effective management of applicable cybersecurity, technology risk, operational resilience, regulatory, legal, and policy requirements within the Business Group. 
 Represent the Business Group during regulatory examinations, supervisory reviews, external assessments and cybersecurity-related audits.  
 Hold leaders accountable to effective remediation of audit findings, regulatory issues, and control deficiencies. 
   Security Integration & Transformation  
 Partner with the enterprise security team to ensure security services and controls meet the needs of the Business Group. 
 Provide security leadership for major initiatives, acquisitions, client commitments, strategic partnerships, and technology transformations, including cyber due diligence, risk assessment, integration planning, and oversight of material remediation commitments. 
 Enable secure adoption of emerging technologies, including cloud, AI, automation, and digital solutions, ensuring appropriate cybersecurity, data protection, privacy, and governance controls are embedded throughout the lifecycle. 
 Provide oversight of information protection, data security, AI security and emerging technology risks ensuring critical information assets are protected and used responsibly and in compliance with regulatory and enterprise requirements.  
 Champion a secure-by-design approach across technology and business initiatives. 
 Incident Preparedness & Resilience  
 Serve as the senior security executive for the Business Group during significant cyber incidents, operational disruptions, and crisis events, coordinating with enterprise incident response, business continuity, legal, privacy, risk, communications, and business leadership to support timely decisions, escalation, recovery and reporting. 
 Oversee the Business Group’s cyber and operational resilience preparedness, including alignment with business continuity and crisis management, scenario testing, crisis simulations, recovery planning and oversight of resulting remediation actions.  
 Oversee the Business Group’s cyber risk assessment program across critical applications, platforms, systems, business processes, and transformation initiatives, ensuring material vulnerabilities, and threats are evaluated, prioritized, and addressed based on business impact and threat-informed analysis. 
 Security Culture & Awareness  
 Foster a strong security culture across the Business Group. 
 Promote accountability for risk management among leaders and employees. 
 Drive awareness and adoption of security best practices. 
 Leadership & Talent Development  
 Lead a network of business-aligned security leaders and professionals from across the Business Group and affiliate entities, providing strategic direction, oversight, and coordination of security priorities within a complex global matrix environment.  
 Present cyber risk, resilience, security posture, and emerging threats to executive committees, governance forums, and board-level audiences as required.  
 Lead through influence across complex matrixed environments. 
 Represent both the enterprise security function and business group with senior executives, regulators, auditors, and within industry forums.  
 Demonstrate executive presence and credibility with senior leaders. 
 Balance risk management with commercial and strategic objectives. 
 Drive informed decision-making under ambiguity and changing conditions. 
 Act as a trusted advisor capable of challenging constructively when risks warrant escalation. 
 Qualifications  
 Education  
 University degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Technology, Risk Management, Business, or a related discipline. 
 Relevant security certifications preferred (CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CGEIT, or equivalent). 
 Experience  
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, risk management, or related disciplines. 
 Experience advising senior global executives on technology and cyber risk matters. 
 Experience operating in highly regulated environments. 
 Proven ability to influence strategic and investment decisions at an executive level. 
 Experience leading large-scale transformation, risk, or security initiatives. 
 Key Knowledge & Skills  
 Deep understanding of information security, cyber risk, regulatory requirements, and resilience frameworks. 
 Strong business acumen and ability to translate technical risks into business impacts. 
 Exceptional stakeholder management and executive communication skills. 
 Strong understanding of enterprise technology, cloud, data, AI, and digital platforms. 
 Strategic leader with the ability to anticipate and address emerging risks and opportunities. 
 Strong judgment, influence, and decision-making capability. 
 Ability to lead through influence in a matrixed global organization. 
 Success Profile  
 The ideal candidate combines the credibility of a security leader with the mindset of a business executive. They are a trusted advisor to senior leaders, capable of enabling growth and innovation while ensuring risks are effectively understood, governed, and managed.

Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

About the Role
 Birg is a holding company that builds companies. Four entities run on one connected system: Birg.co (the holding company), rthmc (the venture studio that takes technology companies from idea to scale), Interuum (the talent pool deployed across the group), and Birg Capital (the capital arm). 
 This role exists for one reason: so the CEO no longer has to be the guy in the room for execution to happen. You will lead the venture studio’s execution across the portfolio, launching concurrent ventures on system and to standard and scaling toward roughly ten live ventures by the end of 2027. You'll work directly with a repeat, exited founder whose leverage belongs on capital, partnerships, and the next opportunity — not on whether Venture 002 shipped on time. That part is yours.
 The machine handles the black-and-white on purpose, which is exactly why you can't be. We're looking for the operator who reads the signal beneath the noise, knows the entrepreneur from the wantpreneur on sight, and has the gravitas to hire and motivate Venture CEOs you'd put in front of a Fortune 500 board. Speed, operating rigor, and founder instinct rarely live in one person. When they do, that's this hire.
 Key Responsibilities
 Own the Machine
 Reach full fluency — fast — in how the group operates: every system, every venture, every gate.
 Own the operating system end to end and hold every venture to its M0 / M1 / M2 stage gates. Nothing progresses on momentum alone.
 Improve the system continuously as patterns emerge across the portfolio.
 Treat adherence to the system as non-negotiable — for yourself and everyone in it.
 Own Venture Execution
 Drive Venture 001 and Venture 002 from readiness to launch; plan and stage Venture 003.
 Make sequencing and prioritization calls independently — which venture to push, which to pause, before the dashboard says so.
 Be accountable for launches, on time and on system — not for tracking projects.
 Report signal, not activity, and surface risk early.
 Recruit & Motivate Venture Leadership
 Attract and hire Venture CEOs (or EIRs, where that's the better model) for Venture 001 and every venture that follows.
 Build the attract kit and compensation architecture that lands founder-caliber talent.
 Bring the gravitas and motivation that keeps venture leaders performing at pace.
 Run the Control Center
 Own the venture studio’s operating cadence: annual planning → quarterly mapping → monthly plans → weekly deliverables.
 Run execution in ClickUp (or equivalent) with real discipline; coordinate leadership calendars and build the rhythms that keep everyone in sync.
 Surface anything blocked or behind before the halfway mark — never at the deadline.
 Ensure each venture has the digital presence required for launch, working with the relevant growth and brand leads.
 Build the Team & the AI Layer
 Assess hiring needs across the portfolio and bring people in with the Head of People (HOP) through the systems already built.
 Default to AI agents before headcount; build and improve the AI operating layer that lets one operator oversee many ventures at once.
 Build lean, high-caliber teams only when the portfolio has earned them.
 Success Metrics
 First 30 days 
 Full fluency in the group and its systems — what's shipped, blocked, and at risk across Venture 001 and 002.
 A weekly operating cadence live across the portfolio.
 By 90 days 
 Birg.co and all subsidiary websites and online presence built and live.
 Venture 001 and 002 execution on track and on system; Venture 003 planned and staged.
 A repeatable reporting framework running; first Venture CEO / EIR search underway, with attract kit and compensation in place.
 6 months 
 Venture leadership placed and performing; hiring flowing through the systems with HOP.
 The control center running the portfolio on a predictable rhythm.
 12 months 
 Execution runs on systems, not on the CEO's oversight.
 Ventures launching on the same playbook, each faster than the last — on the path to ~10 live ventures by the end of 2027.
 The CEO makes portfolio and resourcing calls on your judgment without checking the underlying work.
 Requirements
 Must-Have Experience
 6+ years operating in startups, venture building, or general management — ideally across more than one company.
 Fractional / portfolio COO capability: you've run execution across multiple products or business lines at once, without a large team behind you.
 Owned at least one (ideally several) companies or products from zero to launch — your launch, not someone else's.
 Elite operating discipline: annual → quarterly → monthly → weekly, tracked in ClickUp or equivalent, with blockers escalated early. Authority without drama; clarity as kindness.
 Signal judgment: you separate signal from noise instinctively and know the entrepreneur from the wantrepreneur.
 AI-native: you use AI agents and agentic workflows to replace team-based work, not just to speed up your own.
 Preferred Experience
 Venture studio, startup holding company, PE operating group, or other multi-entity experience.
 Built or scaled a B2B SaaS company.
 Recruited, hired, and managed founder-level talent (CEOs, EIRs).
 Built or directed a company's digital presence and brand from scratch.
 Founder with an exit, now wanting to operate at the portfolio level rather than found again.
 Core Competencies
 Operating Rigor 
 Cadence and systems that make execution predictable.
 Calendar orchestration and early blocker escalation across leadership.
 Venture Judgment 
 Signal-to-noise reading on live ventures.
 M0 / M1 / M2 gate discipline, earned progression, never momentum.
 Leadership Gravitas 
 Recruits and motivates founder-caliber talent.
 Runs teams hard and clean, because clarity is kindness.
 6+ years of experience in startup operations, venture building, general management, or a comparable operating role, ideally spanning more than one company.
 Direct, hands-on experience taking at least one company from zero to launch—not supporting someone else's launch, but owning it.
 Strong working knowledge of AI tools and agentic workflows, with a track record of using them to replace team-based work, not just accelerate individual productivity.
 Experience designing or operating a structured process for de-risking new initiatives—stage gates, funnel management, or comparable venture-building systems.
 Hands-on experience managing execution across multiple workstreams, products, or business lines simultaneously without relying on a large team.
 Experience reporting directly to a CEO or founder, with the judgment to identify and escalate risks early.
 Excellent communication skills, with the ability to provide concise, honest assessments of portfolio or business health.
 Comfortable operating as an independent contractor, with compensation aligned to scope and impact rather than a traditional salary ladder.
 HIGHLY PREFERRED
 Experience within venture studios, startup holding companies, private equity operating groups, or other multi-entity organizations.
 Experience building or scaling a B2B SaaS company.
 Experience implementing structured venture-building frameworks, including stage-gate models, venture operating systems, or similar methodologies.
 Experience with AI agent orchestration, automation platforms, or building AI-native internal tooling.
 Founder experience (successful exit or otherwise) and a desire to operate at the portfolio level rather than founding another company.
 WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE
 Has built more than one company from zero and can clearly explain what changed with each experience.
 Treats venture outcomes as personally owned rather than escalating responsibility upward.
 Defaults to AI agents before requesting additional headcount.
 Gives the CEO bad news early—before it becomes a crisis.
 Can enforce a system rigorously while exercising sound judgment when the system alone isn't enough.
 Builds only the team the portfolio has genuinely earned.
 CANDIDATE SNAPSHOT
 Founder-minded operator with multiple zero-to-one experiences.
 Fluent in AI as a core operating capability, not just a productivity tool.
 Comfortable owning execution across a portfolio with significant autonomy.
 Motivated by building, learning, and compounding impact rather than titles or hierarchy.
 Fully remote. No office, no commute, just you, the operating system, and wherever you do your best work.
 This isn't about inheriting an established company. It's about building and continuously evolving the operating system that future ventures will run on.
 Core collaboration hours: 9:00 AM–12:00 PM PST , ensuring consistent overlap with the founding team.
 Contractor engagement, paid in USD .
 Full compensation details will be shared directly with shortlisted candidates.

 The realpython.com tutorial team is known for making the highest-quality Python tutorials available online. Our mission is to “help Python developers around the world become more awesome.”
 And with a reach of over 3 million visitors a month, it feels amazing how far we’ve come—but we think we can do even better!
 To help us raise the quality level of our tutorials even further, and expand beyond the topics we’ve covered so far, we are looking for authors who:
 Love Python and want to share their knowledge to help learners level up
 Appreciate the importance of clarity and tone in educational writing
 Want to hone their craft and make the most of our extensive publishing process 
 Have the time to start writing one or more new tutorials a month and meet deadlines 
 This is a fully remote position. More info here: realpython.com/jobs/tutorial-writer 
 You should:
 Have a few years of programming under your belt
 Be ready to grow as a writer and work on your writing skills 
 Be comfortable learning brand new topics that you have never done before, which are either not documented or poorly documented
 Have the time to make Real Python a regular part of your week —this will be a significant time commitment and is not easy
 There are plenty of perks to being on the Real Python team:
 Learning: You’ll always be learning something new—and you’ll have fun doing it. You’ll become a better developer, writer, and communicator, while making new friends along the way.
 Eyeballs: Our site gets a lot of traffic—over 3 million visitors per month and growing. We’re regularly featured in other Python publications and we also run one of the largest email newsletters and social media accounts in the community. When you publish a tutorial here, it will get read a lot, and people will love you for it.
 Tutorial Polish: When you submit a tutorial or article to realpython.com, we will personally work with you to polish your work to a high level of quality. In the end, your tutorial will look much better than when you first submitted it, making you look really good.
 Writing Training: When we are done reviewing and editing your tutorial, we will send you detailed feedback on how you can improve your tutorials in the future. This will help you become a better developer, writer, and communicator.
 Personal Exposure: Your picture and bio will be prominently featured on your tutorials and on multiple other places on the site. This can lead to a multitude of new opportunities for you—job offers, freelance projects, and conference invitations. An in-depth tutorial published on Real Python can make a great portfolio piece.
 Get Paid to Learn : You’ll get paid to learn. We’re not asking you to do this “just for the exposure”—this is a paid part-time position.
 Special Opportunities: Members of the tutorial team get access to special opportunities such as contributing to our books and courses, speaking at online meetups we organize, becoming interview guests to chat about an area of your expertise on the Real Python Podcast , working on team projects, and more.
 You’ll Have an Impact: We get emails and comments every day about how our tutorials help our readers write their first Python program, get their learning progress unstuck, or accomplish their career dream of working with Python professionally. This means a lot to us and makes all the hard work worth it. Our most prolific authors have been approached at conferences and meetups by other developers who read their articles—a great conversation starter.
 100% Remote-Friendly: At Real Python you’ll join a remote-first, distributed, and diverse team that spans across the globe.
 Free Stuff: As a final bonus, by joining the tutorial team you will get a lot of free stuff.  The Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) holds a key position responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a robust compliance program to ensure that CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc. (CDS) and the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC) each operate within their applicable legal and regulatory frameworks.  This mandate covers the complete end-to-end compliance framework for both entities. 
 The CCO ensures an integrated compliance strategy by coordinating with the Businesses, Risk Management, Internal Audit and Enterprise Compliance functions, as well as with the TMX General Counsel’s Office. Providing assurance on the effectiveness of post-trade compliance, the CCO reports directly to the Board of Directors and the Vice President, Regulatory Affairs and Enterprise Compliance. 
 Given that CDS and CDCC are recognized clearing agencies and designated systemically important Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs), the CCO is tasked with ensuring strict adherence to applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including those stemming from such federal designation and provincial recognitions.  In this role, the CCO also liaises directly with key regulators. 
 Work Location: We are open to candidates being located in one of the following Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal. 
 Key Accountabilities 
 1. Compliance Strategy & Oversight 
 Ensure the continued development of a strong, credible, robust culture of compliance through leading the function with excellence, practicality, and strong relationships with the businesses, risk management, legal, TMX affiliates, and external stakeholders 
 Assess the overall compliance framework for CDS and CDCC and adapt it to the evolution of the post-trade businesses and their regulatory requirements, accounting for the systemically important nature of these businesses and their similarities and differences; and on an ongoing basis, reassess the compliance framework to ensure it continues to be fit for purpose 
 Serve as a strategic advisor on the compliance impact of changes to post-trade businesses, including changes to rules, risk frameworks and IT infrastructure 
 Maintain and oversee written policies, procedures and controls to ensure compliance with applicable federal and provincial laws, regulations (including National Instruments), Recognition Orders, and Oversight Agreements and international obligations (collectively the Regulatory Requirements), and monitor regulatory and industry trends affecting the FMIs 
 Ensure timely and appropriate review of written policies and procedures is undertaken regarding the operation of the clearing agencies, develop and conduct training and monitoring to ensure policies and procedures are understood and complied with 
 Collaborate with the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) to ensure that compliance risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated within each FMI's overall enterprise risk management framework 
 Lead the management and delivery of annual disclosures against international standards designed to ensure the safety, efficiency, and resilience of clearing, payment, and settlement systems (i.e., the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI)), including ensuring that appropriate senior clearing agency staff are identified to "own" each key consideration of an applicable PFMI principle, that each owner understands and applies the required PFMI assessment methodology, and periodically assessing the PFMI compliance program including by benchmarking against global peers  
 Meet, as appropriate, with staff at the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) and the Bank of Canada (BoC) to discuss compliance matters, coordinate with the General Counsel’s Office and other stakeholders to respond to questions from relevant regulators and maintain relationships with such regulators 
 Act as a trusted advisor on compliance matters to CDS and CDCC, including responding to early warning questions, establishing trust and open communication with the businesses to allow for proactive detection and remediation; and advise business lines on compliance regarding Participants’ and Clearing Members’ adherence to rules, procedures and manuals 
 Coordinate responses to due diligence questionnaires from Participants covering a variety of areas, including AML, KYC, politically exposed persons, cyber security 
 2. Governance & Board Reporting 
 Prepare and certify an Annual Compliance Report assessing the overall health of the compliance programs, including the FMIs ’ compliance with regulatory requirements for submission to the Board and regulators 
 Engage with the relevant Boards as needed regarding , apprising the Board of material non-compliance that poses a risk to market participants or the broader financial system 
 Meet in camera with the Board and/or designated committees, as needed, and at least once annually to discuss the state of the compliance program 
 3. Incident / Crisis Management 
 Monitor and report any breaches of regulatory requirements to applicable stakeholders on a timely basis 
 Respond promptly and assist as needed in incident management or crisis scenarios, coordinating with risk management, legal, business, operations, technology and other internal stakeholders in the execution of post-trade controls, surveillance, incident management and reporting 
 Collaborate with business lines to periodically update recovery and wind-down plans, which ensure systemic stability by detailing how FMIs manage severe stress, allocates uncovered losses, or safely winds down operations, and participate in default management and recovery plan simulations 
 Must Have(s)
